spans.s: Laukākṣa, pl. (Skt. Gr.), n. of a brahmanical school (of the Chandogas): Divy 〔632.23, 25〕. Cf. Lokākṣa.

laukika, adj. (Skt. id.; BHS also like Pali, lokika), with citta, (thought) about the world; said of the Buddha when he concerns himself with the welfare of some person or persons: ˚kam (〔137.16〕 ˚ka-)cittam utpāditam, or utpādaya(n)ti [] (subject, a Buddha or Buddhas) Divy 〔63.11 ff.〕; 〔77.14 ff.〕; 〔137.16〕; 〔161.23 f.〕; in the last contrasted with a Buddhaʼs lokottara (q.v.) citta; MSV 〔i.255.19〕.

laukikāgra- (or ˚grya-) -dharma, m., sg. or pl., prime-in-the-world condition(s), fourth and highest of the nirvedha-bhaga (-bhāgīya), qq.v.: Mvy 〔1215〕 ˚grya-, but Mironov ˚gra-; Sūtrāl. 〔xiv.26〕 comm. ˚gra-; here identified with ānantarya-samādhi; ˚gra-also AbhidhK. LaV-P. 〔vi.167〕.
